# 1 Samuel Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 164v–165r | **Source Image:** 1SA_007_page_001.jpg, 1SA_007_page_002.jpg

---

**1** The men of Kiriath-jearim came and took the ark of the LORD up to Abinadab's house on the hill. They consecrated his son Eleazar to be the guardian of the ark of the LORD.

**2** A long time passed — twenty years in all — with the ark sitting at Kiriath-jearim. During that time, all Israel began to cry out to the LORD in longing.

**3** Then Samuel addressed the whole nation: "If you are truly turning back to the LORD with all your hearts, then get rid of your foreign gods — your Ashtaroth idols, all of them. Set your hearts firmly on the LORD and serve him alone, and he will rescue you from the grip of the Philistines."

**4** So the Israelites threw away their Baals and their Ashtaroth and served the LORD alone.

**5** Then Samuel said, "Gather all Israel at Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD on your behalf."

**6** So they gathered at Mizpah. They drew water and poured it out before the LORD and fasted all that day. There they confessed, "We have sinned against the LORD." And Samuel served as judge over Israel at Mizpah.

**7** When the Philistines heard that Israel had assembled at Mizpah, their warlords marched up to attack them. The Israelites were terrified when they heard the news.

**8** They begged Samuel, "Don't stop crying out to the LORD our God for us! Plead with him to save us from the Philistines!"

**9** Samuel took a nursing lamb and offered it as a whole burnt offering to the LORD. He cried out to the LORD on Israel's behalf, and the LORD answered him.

**10** While Samuel was presenting the burnt offering, the Philistines advanced to attack Israel. But the LORD thundered with a deafening roar against the Philistines that day and threw them into such confusion that they were routed before Israel.

**11** The men of Israel charged out of Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, cutting them down all the way to a point below Beth-car.

**12** Then Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and Shen. He named it Ebenezer — "Stone of Help" — declaring, "Up to this point the LORD has helped us."

**13** So the Philistines were subdued and did not invade Israelite territory again. The hand of the LORD was against the Philistines for the rest of Samuel's lifetime.

**14** The towns that the Philistines had captured from Israel were restored — from Ekron all the way to Gath — along with the surrounding territory. Israel recovered them all from Philistine control. There was also peace between Israel and the Amorites.

**15** Samuel served as judge over Israel for the rest of his life.

**16** Each year he would make a circuit through Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, judging Israel at each of these places.

**17** Then he would return to Ramah, where his home was, and he would judge Israel from there as well. He also built an altar to the LORD at Ramah.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 2 — "cry out to the LORD in longing":** The Hebrew וַיִּנָּהוּ כָּל־בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל אַחֲרֵי יהוה is notoriously difficult. The verb נהה means to lament or mourn. The sense is that the whole house of Israel was pining after the LORD — a deep national groaning that preceded repentance. The twenty-year gap underscores how slowly spiritual awakening came.

**Verse 6 — Pouring out water:** The water-pouring ritual has no parallel elsewhere in the Torah's prescribed worship. It likely symbolizes the pouring out of the heart in repentance (cf. Lamentations 2:19), or perhaps the emptying of self before God. Samuel's role here bridges prophet, priest, and judge — he intercedes, he offers sacrifice, and he adjudicates.

**Verse 10 — "thundered with a deafening roar":** The Hebrew וַיַּרְעֵם יהוה בְּקוֹל־גָּדוֹל uses the verb רעם (to thunder), paired with "a great voice." This is divine warrior language — God himself fights for Israel. The theophanic thunder echoes Sinai and anticipates the storm-language of Hannah's prayer in chapter 2.

**Verse 12 — Ebenezer (אֶבֶן הָעֵזֶר):** Literally "stone of the help." The dynamic rendering includes the translation of the name because its meaning is the whole point of the memorial. This is a deliberate reversal of the Ebenezer disaster in chapter 4, where the ark was captured. What was once a place of defeat becomes a monument to rescue.

**Verse 13 — "The hand of the LORD was against the Philistines":** This phrase (וַתְּהִי יַד־יהוה בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּים) echoes the plague narrative of chapters 5–6, where the LORD's "hand" was heavy upon the Philistines through tumors and panic. The same power that punished them now restrains them permanently.

— PNEUMA
